title: Design System: คลังไอเดีย (Hackathon Idea Bank)

paper.purpose: Page ground everywhere, including sheets and header.

panel.purpose: Quiet section fills, row hover, read-out bar, inactive tab counts.

ink.purpose: Text, primary buttons, active chips, tab underline, score pips, focus ring, upgrade outline.

ink-3.purpose: Tertiary text: numbers, /20, hints, axis labels, placeholders.

line.purpose: Hairline dividers, card borders, empty pips.

on-sunday-red.purpose: Text and icons on Sunday-red fills.

dark.note: Each colorMeta entry carries its dark value in `dark`. Text on Sunday red stays white in both themes.

colorMixes.name: map-sweet-spot
colorMixes.purpose: Sweet-spot wash on the score map.

score-total.purpose: n/20 totals in rows, shortlist and compare.

headline.purpose: Idea name in the detail panel.

view-title.purpose: Shortlist, Compare and Score Map headings.

pitch.purpose: One-line pitch quote in the detail, max 65ch.

body-small.purpose: Row summaries, compare cells, button text.

micro.purpose: SDG chips, tab counts, compact pip labels.

borders.name: hairline
borders.purpose: Row dividers, column rules, card edges.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background changes on controls and rows.

motion.name: tie-slide
motion.purpose: Shortlist ribbon slides down from the knot; removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Tabs become a flex row with full labels; row actions move beside the text.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Filter rail appears; below it filters open in a left sheet.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Detail docks inline as a third column; below it detail opens in a right sheet.

ribbon.tieInset: 4px narrower, 6px shorter than the main ribbon

narrative.overview:
Colour is identity here, the way every Thai reader decodes สีประจำวัน (the colour of each weekday). Each of the seven day colours owns exactly one job, and an idea's identity is worn as a short cut ribbon hanging from the top edge of its row: the upper band says its track, the tail says its score band, and tying a Sunday-red ribbon beside it puts it on the shortlist. Everything else is white paper and near-black ink.

The surface is a working tool for a small team deciding together, so density is moderate: ranked rows with generous vertical rhythm, tabular figures everywhere a number appears, and depth kept in the detail panel rather than the list. The system is flat. There are no shadows and no gradients; structure comes from hairline rules, a pale panel tone, and one heavy ink outline that marks the upgrade plan. Colour appears only on ribbons, track bars, score-map dots, small swatches, and as a faint tint behind a selected row or track.

It rejects the category default of neutral cards with a single indigo accent and a soup of coloured tag pills. Tags here (SDG chips) are colourless outlines; colour is reserved for meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Seven day colours, seven jobs, no overlap; Sunday red means shortlisted and nothing else.
Flat paper and ink; hairline dividers instead of cards for list content.
One Thai UI family (Anuphan) for everything; tabular lining figures on every number.
Selection shown as a colour tint, not as added chrome.
Light and dark themes share the same roles; dark mode lifts each day colour so it reads on charcoal paper.

rules.name: The One Day, One Job Rule
rules.body: Each day colour encodes exactly one thing. A new feature that needs a colour picks a neutral or an ink treatment; it never borrows a day colour for a second meaning.

rules.name: The Reserved Sunday Rule
rules.body: Sunday red appears only where an idea is shortlisted (or on the control that ties it). Errors, warnings, deletes and badges do not use it.

rules.name: The Tint, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: A day colour may cover an area only as a selection tint mixed into paper (8% behind a selected row, 16% behind a selected track). Solid day colour stays on small marks: ribbons, bars, dots, swatches.

rules.name: The Tabular Everything Rule
rules.body: Every number (scores, counts, idea numbers, ranks, axis ticks, SDG numbers) is set with tabular lining figures so columns of scores align.

rules.name: The No Capitals Rule
rules.body: Nothing is uppercased or letter-spaced for effect. Thai has no case, and labels stay in sentence form at small sizes.

rules.name: The Ribbon Hangs From The Edge Rule
rules.body: A ribbon always starts at the top edge of its row or header (negative top margin cancels the padding), so it reads as hanging from the rule above, not floating in the row.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If something needs separation, give it a hairline or a panel tone; if it needs emphasis, give it ink.

dos: Do give every idea its ribbon wherever it appears (list row, detail header, shortlist, compare column), with the track band on top and the score-band tail below.
Do keep each day colour on its one job: Friday blue T1, Saturday purple T2, Thursday orange T3, Sunday red shortlisted, Wednesday green 18+, Monday yellow 15–17, Tuesday pink 14 and below.
Do set every number with tabular lining figures and show totals as "n/20".
Do separate list content with hairlines (`line`) and reserve borders on controls for `line-2`.
Do show selection as a day-colour tint mixed into paper (8% for rows, 16% for rail items) rather than adding outlines or badges.
Do label every estimate as an estimate next to the number it qualifies.
donts: Don't use Sunday red for anything other than shortlisting: not for errors, deletes, alerts or emphasis.
Don't colour SDG chips or other tags; colour is reserved for the day-colour code.
Don't add box-shadows or gradients; separation comes from tone and hairlines.
Don't fill large surfaces with solid day colour or use one as a page or header background.
Don't use Monday yellow as text or icon colour; it is a fill only.
Don't introduce a second typeface, uppercase labels, or letter-spaced captions.
